sentences.text: Learned AGP Ms.Bhumi Gandhi waives service of notice of admission on behalf of respondent-State.

2. These appeals have been filed under Section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, and Section 96 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, challenging the judgment and award passed by the Learned Principal Senior Civil NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3896/2024 JUDGMENT DATED: 06/03/2026 undefined Judge, Modasa, in Land Acquisition Reference (LAR) No. 1794 of 2010, Reference (LAR)
No.1800 of 2010, Reference (LAR) No.1801 of 2010 and Reference (LAR) No.1802 of 2010, dated 13.01.2017, whereby the Learned Reference Court determined the market value of the acquired land at the rate of Rs. 110.70/- per square meter and awarded an additional compensation of Rs.
100.70/- per square meter, along with all permissible benefits.

3. The factual matrix is as under:-
3.1. The land in question pertains to the village of Fantadhirpur, Taluka Bayad,
District Sabarkantha (now Aravalli), which was acquired by the State Authority for the purpose of constructing a lank water canal.
A Section 4 notification was published in the official gazette on 5.08.2008, and a Section 6 notification was published on 30.07.2009.
Subsequently, a Section 11 award was passed by the Special Land Acquisition Officer on 30.04.2010, determining the market value at the rate of Rs. 10 per square meter.

Aggrieved by the said award, an application was filed under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, seeking enhancement of the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3896/2024 JUDGMENT DATED: 06/03/2026 undefined compensation to Rs.
400/- per square meter.

The Learned Reference Court, relying on the decision rendered in LAR No. 501 of 2010 concerning the village of Desaipura, awarded additional compensation, which forms the subject matter of the present appeal.

4. Heard learned advocate Mr.Manish Shah for the Appellant and learned AGP Ms.Bhumi Gandhi for the Defendant-State.
4.1.

The learned advocate Mr.Manish Shah for the appellant submits that the Learned Reference Court erred in relying on the decision rendered in Exh. 12 in LAR No. 501 of 2010 concerning the village of Desaipura.

However, subsequent to the award passed by the learned Reference Court in the present case, a further decision regarding the same village (Desaipura) was rendered, where the market value was determined at the rate of Rs. 422/- per square meter.

The learned advocate Mr.Manish Shah further submits that in LAR Nos. 1 of 2021 to 12 of 2021, which was decided after the judgment in the instant case, the Section 4 notification was published on 04.12.2008.
In contrast, the Section 4 notification in the present case was issued NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3896/2024 JUDGMENT DATED: 06/03/2026 undefined on 05.08.2008.

Learned advocate Mr.Manish Shah contends that, given the similarity of the facts, the market value in this case should also be enhanced in a similar manner to that in LAR Nos. 1 of 2021 to 12 of 2021.

Learned advocate Mr.Manish Shah has also relied on the judgment given in the case of First Appeal No.30 of 2026 and allied matters which is for Reference (LAR) No.1797 of 2010 arising out of the same impugned award wherein, this Court has allowed the appeal by determining the value of land acquired at Raval Mohanbhai Chandaji vs State Of Gujarat (Deleted) on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194976902/
2 Rs.422/- per sq.mtr.
4.2.

sentences.text: The learned AGP Ms.Bhumi Gandhi, on the instructions of the concerned officer, submits that the State has accepted the decision rendered in LAR Nos. 1 of 2021 to 12 of 2021.
Therefore, the learned AGP Ms.Bhumi Gandhi requests that an appropriate order be passed in this matter.

5. Having considered the submissions made by the Learned Advocates for the respective parties and having referred to the judgment passed by the Learned Reference Court in LAR Nos. 1 of 2021 to 12 of 2021, wherein land acquired for an irrigation scheme in the village of NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3896/2024 JUDGMENT DATED: 06/03/2026 undefined Desaipura, Taluka Bayad, District Aravalli, was valued at Rs. 422/- per square meter, this Court finds that there is a common boundary between the villages of Fantadhirpura and Desaipura, as confirmed by the map produced by the Learned Advocate, which was not disputed by the learned AGP.
The only difference in the acquisition proceedings between these two villages is the date of the Section 4 notification, which differs by only four months.

As the State has accepted the decision in LAR Nos. 1 of 2021 to 12 of 2021 concerning Desaipura and no significant difference has been pointed out between the two villages, this Court holds that the market value for the land in Fatandhirpura should be determined at the rate of Rs. 422/- per square meter, consistent with the decision in LAR Nos. 1 of 2021 to 12 of 2021.

6. Accordingly, the claimants in the present case shall be entitled to the difference in the compensation amount, which shall be paid to them within a period of eight weeks from the date of this order, along with all permissible benefits.
7. Resultantly, these appeals are allowed and disposed of NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3896/2024 JUDGMENT DATED: 06/03/2026 undefined accordingly.

8. It is clarified that the claimant would not be entitled for the interest for the delayed period as stated before this Court at the time of passing an order under the application for condonation of delay.

(M. K. THAKKER,J) ARCHANA S. PILLAI Raval Mohanbhai Chandaji vs State Of Gujarat (Deleted) on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194976902/
